methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of only 30 patients with no control arm and heterogeneous combination regimens (AK104+chemo, +anlotinib, +chemo+anlotinib, +chemo+other AAI). Subgroup analyses (PD-L1 n=17, brain mets n=5) are severely underpowered, and there is no adjustment for confounders such as line of therapy despite strong line-dependent efficacy. Authors acknowledge selection bias, small sample, and lack of heterogeneity as limitations. Statistics are limited to Kaplan-Meier/log-rank with no multivariable modeling or multiplicity correction despite many subgroup comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Small single-center retrospective case series (n=30) of off-label bispecific immunotherapy use, mapping to Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is plausible because driver-negative advanced NSCLC represents an unmet need and first-line AK104+chemo+AAI showed mPFS of 13.3 months, but findings are hypothesis-generating only and the authors explicitly call for larger prospective RCTs.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational retrospective cohort, so STROBE applies. Inclusion/exclusion criteria, endpoints (RECIST 1.1, CTCAE v5), follow-up cutoff, and baseline table are described, with ethics approval (No. 2023-SR-847) and informed consent noted. However, there is no explicit STROBE checklist, no sample-size justification, incomplete confounder handling, and no data-availability statement or repository mentioned in the normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim this is the first real-world study of AK104-based combination regimens in driver gene-negative advanced NSCLC, which is a meaningful extension of existing Phase Ib (AK104+anlotinib) and Phase II (AK104 monotherapy) data cited (refs 11, 12, 20). Novelty is modest because similar bispecific (including another retrospective AK104 NSCLC series, ref 20) and dual-checkpoint combinations (CheckMate 227/9LA) already exist; the contribution is incremental real-world evidence rather than a new mechanism or method.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is organized into conventional IMRaD sections and communicates the main findings clearly, with tables and Kaplan-Meier figures referenced. There are minor inconsistencies (e.g., 'Cadolinimab' spelling in the Introduction vs. 'Cadonilimab' elsewhere) and some redundancy in the Discussion (e.g., single-center limitation repeated). Subgroup percentages are occasionally awkwardly phrased but overall readable.

key_strengths: Addresses an unmet need in driver-negative advanced NSCLC using a novel PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific (AK104)
Reports prespecified RECIST 1.1 and CTCAE v5 endpoints with Kaplan-Meier PFS and 95% CIs
Safety profile characterized in detail including irAEs and discontinuations (one grade 3 immune-mediated pancreatitis)
Useful cross-study contextualization against CheckMate 9LA, KEYNOTE-189/407, CameL and ORIENT-11
key_concerns: Very small single-center retrospective cohort (n=30) with no control arm limits causal inference
Heavy subgroup analysis (PD-L1 n=17; brain mets n=5) with no multiplicity correction or multivariable adjustment for line of therapy
No data-availability statement and no sample-size justification; STROBE checklist not explicitly addressed
Heterogeneous regimens and treatment lines confound efficacy comparisons across subgroups
Minor terminology/spelling inconsistency (Cadolinimab vs Cadonilimab) suggests limited copyediting
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent real-world case series with a topical bispecific antibody but methodologically limited by small n, single-center retrospective design, and underpowered subgroup analyses; appropriate for a Tier 3 oncology journal after major revisions.
